Introduction

Understand why normal objects can become emotionally, symbolically, and financially valuable, then practice explaining value with clear B1 English.

Some objects are valuable because they are useful.

A chair is useful because we can sit on it.

A cup is useful because we can drink from it.

A phone is useful because we can call people, take photos, and use the internet.

But other objects feel valuable for a different reason.

They may not be expensive or special by themselves, but they carry a story.

An old watch from a grandfather may not cost much money, but for one family, it can feel priceless.

This lesson looks at a simple but powerful question: why can an ordinary thing feel special?

The answer is not only about money.

It is also about memory, emotion, identity, belief, and story.

Do you own something that is not expensive but still feels important to you?

Have you ever kept a ticket, photo, keychain, or small gift because of a memory?

Would you pay more for an object if a famous person used it?

Do you think people are logical when they decide what something is worth?

Practice

What is the difference between practical value and story value?

Practical value is what an object does, while story value is the meaning it gets from memories, people, places, or events connected to it.

Which kind of value usually matters more to you: practical value or story value?

Practical value matters more to me because.

Story value matters more to me when.

Why can a lucky item change how a person feels?

A lucky item can make a person feel more confident or safe, even if the item does not really change the future.

Have you ever had a lucky item, routine, or place?

I once felt lucky when.

I do not have a lucky item, but I understand it because.

How can an object become more valuable without physically changing?

It can become more valuable when people connect it to an important person, event, or story, and that creates emotion and demand.

Would you pay more for an object if it had an interesting story?

I might pay more if.

I would not pay more because.

Why is the original guitar more valuable than the same guitar from a shop?

The original guitar is more valuable because it was connected to a real famous moment, so people feel it has history and essence.

Would you rather have a perfect copy of a famous object or the real original?

I would choose the original because.

I would choose the copy if.

How can an object gain negative value?

An object can gain negative value when it is connected to a bad person or frightening event, so people feel uncomfortable about it.

Would you use something if you knew it belonged to a terrible person?

I would feel uncomfortable because.

I might use it if.

Why can family objects feel priceless even when they are not expensive?

They can feel priceless because they connect people to family memories, love, identity, and personal history.

What family object or personal object would you want to keep for a long time?

I would like to keep.

It matters to me because.

Why can a place feel special?

A place can feel special because people connect it to an important event, person, story, or memory.

Is there a place you visited that felt special because of its history or story?

What kind of extra value can a brand add to an object?

A brand can add symbolic value, such as style, status, identity, or the feeling of belonging to a certain image.

Do you think branded items are usually worth the higher price?

How can a story make the price of an object rise?

A story can create emotion and desire, and if many people want a rare object, demand can raise the price.

Summary

This topic shows something important about humans.

We do not live only in a world of objects.

We live in a world of meanings.

A thing can have practical value, market value, emotional value, and symbolic value.

Practical value means what it does.

Market value means how much money people will pay.

Emotional value means how it makes us feel.

Symbolic value means the story, status, memory, or identity it carries.

A simple object can become powerful when it is connected to memory, fame, love, fear, history, or identity.

The physical object may stay the same, but its meaning can change.

When meaning changes, people's feelings change.

When many people's feelings change, the market price can change too.
